svg.title: A client who was told 2 days ago about a terminal diagnosis says, 'The lab must have mixed up my results.' The client needs teaching about a new pain medication. Which approach should the nurse use?
svg.desc: A client in denial can still learn concrete, present-focused information, so teaching is limited to what is needed today rather than long-range planning. Restating the prognosis or waiting for acceptance leaves the client without pain control while they work through a stage that may last days or weeks.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Teaching and Grief Stage
Read the situation
A client who was told 2 days ago about a
terminal diagnosis says, 'The lab must
have mixed up my results.' The client
needs teaching about a new pain
medication. Which approach should the
nurse use?
What fits here
Teach only what the client needs right
now, focusing on the immediate use of the
medication
Why it fits
A client in denial can still learn
concrete, present-focused information, so
teaching is limited to what is needed
today rather than long-range planning.
Restating the prognosis or waiting for
acceptance leaves the client without pain
control while they work through a stage
that may last days or weeks.
